title: Can LLM Annotations Replace User Clicks for Learning to Rank?
abstract: arXiv:2511.06635v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large-scale supervised data is essential for training modern ranking models, but obtaining high-quality human annotations is costly. Click data has been widely used as a low-cost alternative, and with recent advances in large language models (LLMs), LLM-based relevance annotation has emerged as another promising annotation. This paper investigates whether LLM annotations can replace click data for learning to rank (LTR) by conducting a comprehensive comparison across multiple dimensions. Experiments on both a public dataset, TianGong-ST, and an industrial dataset, Baidu-Click, show that click-supervised models perform better on high-frequency queries, while LLM annotation-supervised models are more effective on medium- and low-frequency queries. translated_title: 大语言模型标注能否取代用户点击用于学习排序？
translated_abstract: 大规模监督数据对于训练现代排序模型至关重要，但获取高质量的人工标注成本高昂。点击数据已被广泛用作低成本替代方案，随着大语言模型（LLM）的最新进展，基于LLM的相关性标注已成为另一种有前景的标注方式。本文通过在多个维度上的全面比较，研究LLM标注是否能取代点击数据用于学习排序（LTR）。在公共数据集TianGong-ST和工业数据集Baidu-Click上的实验表明，点击监督模型在高频查询上表现更好，而LLM标注监督模型在中低频查询上更有效。进一步分析显示，点击监督模型更擅长捕捉文档级信号，如权威性或质量，而LLM标注监督模型在捕捉查询-文档匹配语义方面更有效。
tldr: 本文通过多维度对比发现，LLM标注和点击数据在学习排序中各有优势，LLM标注不能完全取代点击数据，但在中低频查询上表现更佳。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals through multi-dimensional comparisons that LLM annotations and click data have complementary strengths in learning to rank, with LLM annotations excelling on medium- and low-frequency queries but not fully replacing click data.
